about: Owner-declared entries of the v5 resolve / traverse deploy gate (gate_policy.py --declared): what the MCP surface cannot show (carried over from declared_v4_rt.json section 1, approved by the owner on 2026-10-14; the scenario ids are v5's, which keep v4's), and the scenarios whose property is inherently time-dependent (budget_stress, lane V5: new, for the owner's review before the freeze). The v4 suite errors of declared_v4_rt.json (T-labels-0004, T-budget-0003, T-attempts-0002 r1, REL-prefix_equals-0001/0002/0003) are fixed by v5 and not carried. Decided by the owner, never inferred from an answer a run received; each entry names its evidence.

exclusions.reason: the MCP's traverse_capabilities answers the service's view (gate, backends, service_maxima, presets), not the host's document (table case capabilities.traverse_capabilities_document: 'the raw document and its gate-block projection are not exposed'), so its one property check, capabilities_doc, is not exposed ('field not in the answer: release') and every MCP execution is inconclusive; nothing else is tested there. Tested on direct-local.

budget_stress (lane V5, item 5; triage-v4 V05): the property, a stated /resolve stop answering the resolve of the query's prefix, needs the row batch in flight at the work deadline (budget - 250 ms) to end before the budget, which depends on the batch times, i.e. on the host's load and on what is warm; no budget makes a stop certain (v3 and v4: no stop in any answer), so the scenario cannot be decisive under load. It follows its complete twin (R-twin-0002, the warm-up, required) and runs in the full suite; its relation REL-prefix_equals-0001 leaves the gate with it. Excluded on MCP already (a query above the MCP's 2,000 bp).

not_required.reason: the MCP's traverse records carry no label dictionary ('field not in the answer: results[0].label_dict' on every MCP execution of v3 and v4, VERIFY-B); the walk itself (walk_in_record) stays required on the MCP arm, label_dict_contains on direct-local.

the service merges identical seeds before sending (table case traverse.duplicate_seeds), so the duplicate's result (results.1.duplicate) cannot exist in the MCP answer; the merge itself is the by-design pair direct-local verifies, answer_fields stays required on direct-local.
